text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.2% today to $367.19, extending a sharp two-week decline of 1.5%. The stock has dropped roughly 11% since mid-November, tracking a significant selloff in oil refining stocks that follows crude oil sliding from around $80 to roughly $90 per barrel over the same period. While U.S. oil prices stabilized near $89.50 today, the refining sector's weakness reflects the reality that lower crude prices shrink margins—the difference between what refiners pay for raw oil and what they sell refined products for—even as refinery utilization remains healthy at 95.7%.

The geopolitical tensions between Iran, Saudi Arabia, and Bahrain reported today didn't reverse the downward momentum, suggesting markets have already priced in oil supply risk. The permitting reform bill that passed the Senate could eventually ease long-term energy infrastructure costs, but those gains lie too far ahead to support refiner valuations in the face of near-term margin pressure from lower crude costs and ample product inventories—gasoline storage remains elevated at 216 million barrels.
